items.title: Ari Emanuel’s Mari Acquires Broadway and West End Theater Owner ATG Entertainment
items.summary:
Ari Emanuel's live events company Mari has agreed to buy ATG Entertainment, the theater group that owns venues on Broadway and in London's West End, from private equity firm Providence Equity. The companies did not disclose financial terms, though The Hollywood Reporter pegged the deal at roughly $6 billion. The transaction still requires regulatory approval.

ATG is the third-largest owner of Broadway houses with seven theaters, behind the Shubert Organization's 17 and the Nederlander Organization's nine. It reached that position by acquiring a majority stake in Jujamcyn Theaters in 2023, the last major transaction of its kind on Broadway. Its holdings include the Lyric Theatre, home of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, plus 10 West End venues among them the Lyceum, where The Lion King runs, and the Savoy, home to Paddington the Musical.

In total, ATG owns, operates or programs 70 venues across Britain, the United States, Germany, Austria and Spain. Providence Equity bought its majority stake for about $500 million in 2013 from Exponent Private Equity. Reports of a possible sale first surfaced in June.

The purchase deepens Mari's position in theater following its October 2025 acquisition of ticketing company TodayTix, which came shortly after Mari itself launched. The company's other holdings include the Miami Open and Madrid Open tennis events, the Frieze art fairs and auction house Barrett-Jackson. Emanuel also serves as CEO of TKO, the parent of WWE and UFC, and executive chairman of WME Group.

"I've spent my whole career in entertainment, and I started out in theater. I've seen the industry reinvent itself many times, but live has only grown more powerful," Emanuel said. "This is a long-term bet on where live goes next." Producer Sonia Friedman, an ATG producing partner behind Paddington and Cursed Child, said what she finds compelling about Mari is "its breadth of experience across live events and its respect for creative independence."

Once the deal closes, ATG will keep its existing brand and leadership and maintain what the companies described as its commitment to creative independence.

items.title: ZZ Top Drummer Frank Beard Battling Serious Health Issues: Report
items.summary:
ZZ Top drummer Frank Beard is dealing with serious health issues, TMZ reported, as noted by Consequence. The news follows the band's cancellation of its August 5th concert at the Hollywood Bowl, which the group attributed to unforeseen personnel matters and insurmountable obstacles.

That Los Angeles show was meant to open the band's headlining summer tour, which features rotating support from Cheap Trick, George Thorogood and the Destroyers and other acts. Michael Monahan has been filling in on drums since the cancellation and is expected to continue in the role.

Beard has played with ZZ Top since 1969. He stepped away last year to address foot and ankle problems, with his longtime drum tech John Douglas and Monahan splitting the duties in his absence. He rejoined the band in September 2025 and had been performing with them until this latest setback.

With Beard out, singer-guitarist Billy Gibbons is the only original member in the touring lineup. Bassist Dusty Hill died in 2021 and was replaced by his guitar tech, Elwood Francis.

The tour resumes Tuesday, August 11th, in Redmond, Washington, and runs through an October 9th date in Port Wentworth, Georgia.

items.title: Spotify to Label AI Artists on the Platform With New ‘AI Persona’ Badge
items.summary:
Spotify will begin attaching an "AI Persona" badge to artist profiles it identifies as AI-generated, with the label rolling out in mid-September. Music from artists carrying the badge will be excluded from the platform's personalized recommendations. Creators can start disclosing that a profile is AI-generated on Tuesday, August 11.

Billboard reported that Spotify will not rely on voluntary disclosure alone. The company plans to review accounts itself, and artists flagged that way can either self-disclose or file an appeal. The badge will indicate which route applied, showing listeners whether the artist volunteered the information or Spotify made the determination. Spotify says it will let listeners report accounts as AI in the coming months.

The label targets the public identity of an artist rather than the production of any individual track. That distinction matters because Spotify already built tools for the song level: an AI credits feature launched in April, initially for DistroKid users, lets artists disclose which parts of a recording used AI. Later that month the company introduced "Verified by Spotify," a badge marking human artists, and in March it rolled out Artist Profile Protection, an optional setting that lets artists review releases before they appear on their profiles.

The moves follow sustained pressure from the recorded music business. In July, the RIAA, IFPI, the American Association of Independent Music and other trade groups proposed a two-tier system distinguishing "AI-generated" songs from "AI-assisted" ones. Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Sony Music, HYBE, Believe and Concord separately proposed eligibility rules for AI songs on charts, and IFPI said the next day it would adopt those principles for charts it manages.

Spotify is pursuing AI in other directions at the same time. The company recently struck deals with Universal Music Group and Merlin to permit AI remixes and covers of songs by artists on their rosters, offered as a paid add-on for premium subscribers.

items.title: Shabazz Palaces Readying New Album It’s a Style Sport
items.summary:
Ishmael Butler will release a new Shabazz Palaces album, It's a Style Sport, on October 23 through Sub Pop. The record follows his back-to-back mini-albums Exotic Birds of Prey and Robed in Rareness.

Butler produced the album with Erik Blood. Contributors include Marquette Miller, Thaddillac, Evan Flory-Barnes, Gerald "Tugboat" Turner, Kassa Overall and Carlos Overall.

Pitchfork reported that the ten-track album is led by the single "Ahh World (I Won the Alpha Bet)," which is out now. The rest of the tracklist runs through "Field Notes," "Show Me Missouri in Mink," "Jheri Curl Jump," "Deadstock Dude," "Tongue in Chic," "Heliocentric Immortality Manifesto H.I.M.," "Olivia According to Touch," "Money Can't Save Your Mind" and "From One Future to Another."

items.title: David Ellison Threatens to Pull Paramount Out of California Starting Oct. 1 if States Refuse to Negotiate Settlement in Antitrust Suit
items.summary:
David Ellison has told Paramount's senior executives he is prepared to begin moving the company out of California on October 1 if state Attorney General Rob Bonta does not agree to settlement talks in the antitrust suit filed by 12 states to block the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery merger. Ellison said the Paramount Skydance board has already approved the move, which would extend to Warner Bros. as well should the merger close. Variety confirmed the account with sources; the threat was first reported by the newsletter Puck.

Ellison laid out the plan at an August 5 meeting on the Paramount lot with his 12-member senior team, which included studio chiefs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein and CBS and TV media chair George Cheeks. He told the group he expects Paramount to win the antitrust case. The Los Angeles headquarters would leave the state first, with tax incentives from other states helping cover relocation costs, followed by a five-year plan to shift most studio jobs out of California.

The October 1 date is not arbitrary. That is when Paramount begins accruing a ticking fee of $7 million per day payable to Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders. With trial in the states' suit scheduled to begin March 2, 2027, Paramount would owe roughly $1.2 billion by the time proceedings wrap. Those payments are not due until the deal closes.

Bonta has not said publicly what concessions would satisfy him, though he has indicated any remedy would need to be structural, meaning divestments, rather than behavioral measures such as production quotas. Paramount declined to comment on Ellison's plans.

The company has not settled on a destination, with Georgia, Texas and Tennessee among those under consideration. Some executives at the August 5 meeting were caught off guard by the timeline, and a large-scale departure could trigger resignations, particularly with substantial layoffs expected if the Warners merger closes. Paramount Skydance employed about 17,600 people worldwide at the end of 2025; Warner Bros. Discovery had 35,500.

Paramount has lined up $24 billion in commitments from the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates to help finance the takeover, giving the three funds 38.5% of the combined company. In SEC filings, Paramount has argued no U.S. government review of the financing is warranted because those investors would hold no board seats or voting shares. The company still lists 1515 Broadway in New York as its principal executive offices, though Ellison and much of his team work from the Melrose Avenue lot in Hollywood.
